newsitem.title: USA: New Orleans judge certifies tobacco class.
newsitem.headline: New Orleans judge certifies tobacco class.

text.p: A civil district judge in New Orleans has certified a state class action lawsuit brought by Louisiana smokers against the tobacco industry, plaintiffs lawyers said Wednesday.

Lawyers said the ruling marked the first certification of a state tobacco class action growing out of what is known as the Castano federal class action case, which was dismissed by the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals last year. After the federal appeals court action, lawyers in the Castano case began filing suits in state courts.

In the current ruling in Scott v. American Tobacco Co., Judge Richard Ganucheau of the Civil District Court for the Parish of Orleans held that a class be certified of Louisiana smokers who want to participate in medical monitoring and smoking cessation programs.
The judge also reserved the class members' rights to assert any claims for damages they may have suffered as a result of smoking.
The class will be made up of residents who are or were smokers on or before May 24, 1996.
Plaintiffs lawyers estimated that nearly one million Louisiana residents are included in the class.
The judge has ordered the lawyers to submit a notice for his review that will inform potential class members of their right to participate in the smoking cessation or monitoring programs.
